title: How Self-Aware Are You
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article positions self-awareness as arguably the single strongest predictor of lifetime leadership success, defining it as the ability to see one's own strengths and weaknesses objectively and to recognize the gap between self-perception and how others actually see you. The author describes highly self-aware leaders as constantly reading the contrast between their own view and others' reactions, then using that data to adapt their behavior in real time. Practical suggestions include examining core values against respected peers and actively soliciting feedback about blind spots. The piece closes by invoking the ancient Greek maxim that self-knowledge is the beginning of wisdom.
points: Self-awareness may be the single best predictor of long-term leadership success.
It hinges on recognizing the gap between how you see yourself and how others actually perceive you.
Highly self-aware leaders constantly read that contrast and adapt their behavior based on it.
Concrete steps include comparing your values against respected peers and actively soliciting feedback about blind spots.
quotes: If there were only one quality from which to predict lifetime success, self-awareness would have to be on the shortlist.
They have an objective view of their strengths and their weaknesses.
Perhaps most importantly, they understand the contrast between how they see themselves and how others see them.
They judge their accuracy by observing how others respond to their choices in style, messages, actions, and decisions.
The best leaders agree with the ancient Greeks that knowing yourself is the beginning of wisdom.
